title: World Models Need Causality, Not Pretty Pixels — Christopher Manning, Moonlake AI
talk_summary: Christopher Manning recounts AI/NLP history and presents Moonlake AI's approach to embodied AGI: building action-conditional world models as neurosymbolic simulations where code (physics engines, object models) underlies generative rendering, rather than pixel-only video generators. The core mechanism is a code-generation loop that renders objects, compares against real observations, and revises code to shrink the sim-to-real gap.

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate code that renders a scene, compare the render against real-world observation, compute deviations, then revise the code iteratively — an automated closed loop with a concrete fidelity metric.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We can then assess how good our render is against physical reality and then we can work out the deviations. We can revise the code

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the controllable/verifiable part of the system in explicit symbolic form (code, object models) so it can be inspected, edited, and maintained by humans and other systems, rather than opaque latent state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the symbolic representation can be easily interfaced controlled edited and maintained in our human world

takeaways.what_they_do: When an observation is partial (closed tea box), they fetch external info via RAG to fill in the hidden structure before simulating.

takeaways.technique: Simulation to generate training/eval data cheaply
takeaways.what_they_do: Use simulation to get large volumes of cheap scenario data instead of expensive real-world collection, targeting rare/tail cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can instead build accurate simulations which will allow transfer to real
